messages:
Maya K: Quick sync — are we aligned on a single trace field in logs across services? I keep seeing trace_id / trace.id / traceId and it's wrecking our log->trace joins in the console.

Arun S: We discussed this in infra last sprint. Recommendation was to standardize on trace.id (dot) to match OTEL semantic conventions. Short story: use trace.id everywhere and normalize ingest for legacy.

Priya R: +1 for OTEL semantic names. Question: do we want services to inject trace.id at emission time, or enrich at the collector/extraction layer?

Ben L: Prefer enrichment at the collector when possible so we don't have to change every service. But that only works if the trace context is present on the incoming request. Backgrounded async jobs and worker logs are trickier.

Zoe T: From a dashboards POV, having trace.id in emitted logs makes UI linking immediate and cheap. If it's only in enriched events, the link latency increases and we have edge cases where enrichment failed.

Maya K: Right. Tradeoffs: SDK changes vs pipeline complexity. Also retention/cost: adding fields to our indexed logs increases size and query cost. We need to quantify.

Priya R: Security question — any PII risk from copying trace fields? Usually no, but some customers put user IDs in span attributes. We should strip attributes and only use trace.id (and maybe span.id) for links.

Arun S: Agreed. Implementation idea: 1) standardize trace field name to trace.id; 2) update internal logging libs (go/python/node) to emit trace.id if present; 3) collector enrichment: if no trace header but incoming request has context, add trace.id; 4) retention: keep trace fields in raw blob but only index trace.id.

Ben L: For the collector config, here's a minimal otelcol processors pipeline we tried in staging:
```yaml
processors:
  batch:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: trace.id
        action: insert
        value: "${trace_id}"
service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [redwood-loki]
```
This inserts when available. It won't synthesize a trace id for non-traced requests.

Maya K: That looks good. We should also push a change to our logging shim to do:
```python
# pseudo
if span := trace.get_current_span():
    record['trace.id'] = span.context.trace_id
```
so services opt-in quickly.

Zoe T: For dashboarding/backfills: we'll need a small migration job to map trace_id/traceId -> trace.id for the last 90 days. Can we run this at query-time via a join or do bulk reindexing? Bulk reindexing is expensive.

Priya R: Query-time normalization is cheaper initially: treat trace.id OR trace_id OR traceId as equivalent when building links. We'll add a parser rule in the console backend to check multiple fields before falling back.

Arun S: We'll do a canary: enable SDK emission for internal services in dev, enable collector attribute insertion in staging, and add console query-time normalization for prod. After 2 weeks of metrics - if <0.1% failed joins - we flip internal SDKs in prod.

Ben L: Also need to update our OTLP exporter retention settings. There's an edge where exporters add attributes and those expanded logs increase storage. I'm proposing we store the enriched blob for 14d full-text, then compact to JSON blob with only indexable fields preserved for 90d.

Maya K: Good call. Can you draft the retention policy? We need to show finance delta before we commit.

Ben L: Draft: full-text enriched logs (with trace.id) 14d, indexed trace.id + timestamp + service 90d, archive raw to cold storage 365d. Estimate +3.2% storage cost for 90d window. Will confirm.

Zoe T: Also add a small telemetry event when a link is clicked in the console so we can measure user impact (click-to-trace success rate). That'll help justify cost.

Priya R: Rollout checklist suggestion:
- update logging SDKs (go/python/node) with feature flag
- collector attribute insert enabled for staging
- console query-time normalization merged
- small backfill script for last 30d (non-blocking)
- metric: join_success_rate, average_link_time

Maya K: Love it. @observability-bot can you create a tickets epic and link the SDK PRs? Also assign Ben for retention numbers and Zoe for dashboard changes.

observability-bot: Created epic OBS-762: "Standardize trace field and log enrichment" and linked PRs: repo/logging-shims#449, infra/otel-config#112.

Arun S: One more note — let's pick canonical header names we expect: traceparent / tracestate for W3C, and also x-cloud-trace-context for some legacy GCP libs. Collector should canonicalize these to the OTEL context before insertion.

Maya K: Great. Timeline: aim for canary next week, staging rollout after QA, prod SDK flip the week after if metrics look good. I'll coordinate and post updates here. :thumbsup:
